pictures.scene: Hendrick ter Brugghen, King David Playing the Harp — the old king in his crown and gold brocade robe with his hand laid on the strings and the singers crowded in behind him, for the choirmaster of David, the fool says in his heart
pictures.name: pd_brugghen_king_david

pictures.scene: The Laughing Fool — the jester in his yellow eared hood laughing with his hand spread over one eye and his bauble lifted behind his shoulder, there is no God, they are corrupt their acts are vile
pictures.name: pd_the_laughing_fool

pictures.scene: Jan van Eyck, God Almighty — the enthroned figure in the jewelled triple crown and red robe looking straight out, gold rays and gold lettering filling the arch behind Him, there is no one who does good, the LORD looks down from heaven
pictures.name: pd_van_eyck_god_almighty

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Tower of Babel — the tower rising in tiers of arches, half pale stone and half raw brick, with scaffolding and tiny workmen over all of it and stonecutters at their blocks below, upon the sons of men, to see if any understand
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_tower_of_babel

pictures.scene: Frederick McCubbin, Lost — a child in a straw hat standing alone in the dry scrub among the pale gum trunks with one hand up to her face, if any seek God, all have turned away
pictures.name: pd_mccubbin_lost

pictures.scene: Caravaggio, The Cardsharps — the young player studying his cards over the board while the older man in the striped sleeve leans in behind him to read the hand, they have together become corrupt, there is no one who does good
pictures.name: pd_caravaggio_the_cardsharps

pictures.scene: Adriaen Brouwer, Peasant Brawl — the man drawing his knife outside the inn while the woman in the white kerchief holds him back, the jug and the pot still standing on the bench beside them, not even one, will the workers of iniquity never learn
pictures.name: pd_brouwer_peasant_brawl

pictures.scene: Jean-Francois Millet, The Gleaners — two women bent double over the stubble picking up the few ears left to them, one in a blue bonnet and one in a red cap, while the whole harvest is stacked and carted away behind them, they devour my people like bread, they refuse to call upon the LORD
pictures.name: pd_millet_the_gleaners

pictures.scene: John Martin, Belshazzar's Feast — the prophet standing up in dark robes among the banqueters and pointing, the whole hall flinging up their arms over the laden table and the great tower going dark under the storm, there they are overwhelmed with dread, for God is in the company of the righteous
pictures.name: pd_john_martin_belshazzars_feast

pictures.scene: Jacob van Ruisdael, The Castle of Bentheim — the castle with its towers and green roofs standing on the wooded crag above the cottages, two small travellers on the path below it, you sinners frustrate the plans of the oppressed, yet the LORD is their shelter
pictures.name: pd_ruisdael_the_castle_of_bentheim

pictures.scene: Gustav Bauernfeind, Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives — a party of travellers halted on the stony road in the valley, looking across at the walled city with its domes and towers catching the evening light, oh that the salvation of Israel would come from Zion, when the LORD restores His captive people
pictures.name: pd_bauernfeind_zion

pictures.scene: Solomon Alexander Hart, The Feast of the Rejoicing of the Law — the men in their prayer shawls carrying the dressed Torah scrolls in procession through the synagogue while the congregation watches from the gallery above, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad
pictures.name: pd_hart_rejoicing_of_the_law

lines.text: For the choirmaster. Of David.
The fool says in his heart,
“There is no God.”
They are corrupt; their acts are vile.
There is no one who does good.
The LORD looks down from heaven
upon the sons of men
to see if any understand,
if any seek God.
All have turned away,
they have together become corrupt;
there is no one who does good,
not even one.
Will the workers of iniquity never learn?
They devour my people like bread;
they refuse to call upon the LORD.
There they are, overwhelmed with dread,
for God is in the company of the righteous.
You sinners frustrate the plans of the oppressed,
yet the LORD is their shelter.
Oh, that the salvation of Israel would come from Zion!
When the LORD restores His captive people,
let Jacob rejoice,
let Israel be glad!
